title: iSON Group commits fresh $75-M outlay for PH expansion, more jobs

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — An Indian conglomerate is investing $75 million (P4.7 billion) in new and expanded Philippine operations expected to generate about 2,000 jobs, as President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. sought to attract more investments during his visit to India.

The commitment from iSON Group covers agricultural technology, healthcare, business process outsourcing (BPO) and digital infrastructure, Trade Secretary Maria Cristina Roque said, according to a statement issued by the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) on Sunday.
The investment includes a proposed $50-million agro-solar project, healthcare and 24/7 teleconsultation services, and a $10-million expansion of BPO and global delivery centers.
Roque said iSON’s planned investments aligned with the administration’s priorities, particularly food security and the expansion of digital services.
“They want to improve technology in the agriculture sector,” Roque said after Marcos’ meetings with Indian business executives at the Taj Mahal Hotel in New Delhi on Saturday.
“Agriculture and food security are among the main priorities of the president, so any advancement in agricultural technology is important to the country,” she added.

President Marcos is in India for a two-day visit to attend the 18th BRICS Summit, where he is expected to hold a bilateral meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He was invited to the summit in his capacity as chairman of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean).
The proposed teleconsultation service could also help address the shortage of healthcare access in remote and geographically isolated communities, Roque said.
The service is expected to cost about P65 a month and would allow patients to consult doctors online at any time, although final implementation details have yet to be determined.
“We are a country of 7,600 islands, so sometimes it is difficult to consult a doctor, especially when the nearest facility is in another town,” Roque said.
The planned expansion would add to iSON Group’s existing Philippine operations.
Its digital infrastructure arm, iSON Tower Ltd. Inc., has operated in the country since 2021 under the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s Common Tower Policy.
The company has invested around $65 million in the Philippines and deployed about 450 telecommunications towers serving approximately 600 tenants across Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao.
In August, iSON said it is planning to invest $250 million in agricultural and solar projects in addition to its ongoing $300-million telecommunications tower rollout. /dl
